papers.title_zh: 未经管理的塑料废物显着增加登革热负担
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Plastic pollution is increasingly recognized as a global environmental challenge, yet its role as a measurable driver of infectious disease risk remains poorly quantified. We developed a material-specific extension of the WHO-recommended Breteau Index (BI) that incorporated discarded waste into routine Aedes larval surveillance and evaluated its ability to explain dengue risk using nationwide surveillance data from Sri Lanka. We found that discarded non-biodegradable waste represented a major breeding habitat associated with dengue transmission, with plastic containers comprising the dominant material fraction. Waste-associated breeding habitats accounted for 30–34% of reported dengue burden nationally during 2024–2025. An empirically derived material-partitioning approach further estimated that plastic-associated habitats contributed approximately 22–23% of dengue burden across sentinel districts. Together, this material-specific surveillance framework translates unmanaged environmental waste into measurable infectious disease risk, providing a practical indicator instrument for both downstream vector surveillance and upstream waste-management and plastic policies.

papers.title: Molecular detection of Coxiella burnetii in suspected dengue patients from the Bauru region, São Paulo State, Brazil.
papers.abstract: Q fever, caused by Coxiella burnetii, is an underdiagnosed zoonosis in Brazil due to its non-specific clinical presentation and limited diagnostic capacity. This study investigated the molecular detection of C. burnetii in serum samples from patients with acute febrile illness initially suspected of dengue in 34 municipalities of São Paulo State, Brazil. A total of 300 serum samples collected over a three-year period from patients with suspected dengue fever were analyzed. Only samples obtained from patients presenting with up to seven days of febrile illness were included. All samples tested negative for dengue, leptospirosis, and brucellosis and were analyzed by real-time PCR targeting the IS1111 gene. burnetii DNA was detected in 1.3% (4/300) of the samples (95%CI: 0.37%-3.35%), compatible with recent infection during the early symptomatic phase. This study represents the second report of molecular detection of C. burnetii in patients with acute febrile syndrome in Brazil and the first one in São Paulo State. Previous serological studies indicate widespread exposure to the pathogen, highlighting the complementary roles of molecular and serological approaches. These findings support the inclusion of Q fever in the differential diagnosis of undifferentiated febrile illnesses and suggest that One Health-oriented surveillance strategies may help reduce underdiagnosis in Brazil, although further studies with larger sample sizes are needed to confirm this recommendation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 这项研究旨在解决巴西 Q 热诊断不足的问题,由于非特异性症状和有限的诊断工具,伯内特立克克斯体感染经常被忽视。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究分析了三年来从巴西圣保罗州 34 个城市收集的疑似 登革热 患者的血清样本,重点关注那些发烧时间长达 7 天的患者。
elements_zh.methods: 使用标准方法对所有样本进行登革热、钩端螺旋体病和布鲁氏菌病检测,然后通过针对 IS1111 基因的实时 PCR 进行分析,以检测伯内氏立克次体。
elements_zh.main_results: 在 1.3% (4/300) 的样本中检测到伯氏柯克斯体 DNA (95%CI: 0.37%-3.35%),表明在早期症状阶段有近期感染。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,在鉴别未分化发热性疾病的 诊断 时应考虑 Q 热,因为分子检测显示,之前在疑似登革热病例中存在未被充分报告的伯内特立克次体。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果凸显了将分子方法纳入巴西发热性疾病 监测 策略的必要性,这可能会改善 Q 热的检测并为 One Health 方法提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的证据因其侧重于特定地理区域的分子检测和相对较小的样本量而受到限制,这可能会影响普遍性。这些发现的可信度是中等的。

papers.abstract_zh: 由伯内特立克克斯体引起的 Q 热在巴西是一种诊断不足的 人兽共患病,因为其临床表现非特异性且诊断能力有限。本研究调查了巴西圣保罗州 34 个城市最初怀疑患有登革热的急性发热性疾病患者血清样本中伯内特念珠菌的分子检测。对三年内从疑似 登革热 患者收集的总共 300 份血清样本进行了分析。仅包括从发烧长达 7 天的患者获得的样本。所有样本的登革热、钩端螺旋体病和布鲁氏菌病检测均为阴性,并通过针对 IS1111 基因的实时 PCR 进行分析。在 1.3% (4/300) 的样本中检测到伯内特氏菌 DNA (95%CI: 0.37%-3.35%),这与早期症状阶段的近期感染相符。这项研究是巴西急性发热综合征患者中伯内特念珠菌分子检测的第二份报告,也是圣保罗州的第一份报告。先前的血清学研究表明广泛接触病原体,强调了分子和血清学方法的互补作用。这些发现支持将 Q 热纳入未分化发热性疾病的鉴别诊断 诊断 中,并表明以单一健康为导向的 监测 策略可能有助于减少巴西的漏诊率,尽管需要更大样本量的进一步研究来证实这一建议。

papers.title: Correlation of NS1 Antigen and Dengue Virus Serotype with Infection Status in Dengue Patients
papers.abstract: Non-structural protein 1 (NS1) antigen is an important biomarker for the early diagnosis of dengue virus infection. However, NS1 detection may be influenced by dengue virus serotype and the host immune response during primary and secondary infections, with inconsistent findings reported across previous studies. To investigate the association between NS1 antigen positivity, dengue virus serotypes, and infection status in patients with RT-PCR-confirmed dengue infection. An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted among 65 hospitalized patients with RT-PCR-confirmed dengue infection. Blood samples were collected within the first five days after fever onset (median, 3 days; range, 1–5 days). papers.title_zh: NS1抗原和登革病毒血清型与登革热患者感染状况的相关性
papers.source_body_en: Non-structural protein 1 (NS1) antigen is an important biomarker for the early diagnosis of dengue virus infection. However, NS1 detection may be influenced by dengue virus serotype and the host immune response during primary and secondary infections, with inconsistent findings reported across previous studies. To investigate the association between NS1 antigen positivity, dengue virus serotypes, and infection status in patients with RT-PCR-confirmed dengue infection. An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted among 65 hospitalized patients with RT-PCR-confirmed dengue infection. Blood samples were collected within the first five days after fever onset (median, 3 days; range, 1–5 days). Dengue virus serotypes were identified using the STANDARD M10 Arbovirus Panel, while infection status was determined using the STANDARD F Dengue IgM/IgG fluorescence immunoassay. Associations between NS1 antigen positivity, dengue virus serotypes, and infection status were analyzed using Fisher's exact test. Among 65 RT-PCR-confirmed cases, 55 (84.6%) were NS1-positive, and 10 (15.4%) were NS1-negative. Serotype distribution was DENV-1 (36.9%), DENV-2 (21.5%), DENV-3 (29.2%), DENV-4 (9.2%), and mixed DENV-2/DENV-3 infection (3.1%). No significant associations were found between NS1 antigen positivity and dengue virus serotypes (p = 0.969) or infection status (p = 0.456). Although NS1 positivity was higher in primary than secondary infections (86.4% vs. 66.7%), the difference was not statistically significant. NS1 antigen positivity was not significantly associated with dengue virus serotypes or infection status. The high NS1 positivity observed in this study may reflect early specimen collection during the acute phase of illness, regardless of infection status or viral serotype.

papers.title: The methodological quality of dengue clinical practice guidelines globally. A systematic review.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to systematically review the methodological quality of dengue clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) available globally. METHODS: This systematic review included CPGs on dengue clinical management (clinical diagnosis, investigation and treatment), and the development process of the guidelines, required to be evidence-based and including an expert review process. An electronic search was performed using Google, Google Scholar and PubMed. The search was last performed in September 2025. No language restriction was imposed. The selection of CPGs and cross-checking of data extracted were performed by two independent reviewers with a third to resolve any discrepancies. The Appraisal of Guidelines for Research and Evaluation II (AGREE-II) was used to assess the quality of CPGs by four independent reviewers. RESULTS: A total of 29 CPGs published from 2009-2025 in 18 countries were included for review. Overall, six CPGs rated as high quality. Among these six CPGs, only three reported the recommendations with GRADE. Four CPGs adapted other CPGs without transparent review process. Majority of the CPGs fail to demonstrate a robust scientific development process. CONCLUSION: Despite the variability in the quality of the CPGs assessed in this review, several high-quality guidelines were identified as suitable for use. In contrast, a number of CPGs were found to rely heavily on adaptations of existing guidelines while lacking sufficient methodological rigour. Therefore, CPGs that adapt recommendations from other sources should still undertake a full and systematic development process consistent with the AGREE II framework.

The study included 29 CPGs from 18 countries published between 2009-2025, evaluated using the AGREE-II framework. Majority of the CPGs fail to demonstrate a robust scientific development process. CONCLUSION: Despite the variability in the quality of the CPGs assessed in this review, several high-quality guidelines were identified as suitable for use. In contrast, a number of CPGs were found to rely heavily on adaptations of existing guidelines while lacking sufficient methodological rigour. Therefore, CPGs that adapt recommendations from other sources should still undertake a full and systematic development process consistent with the AGREE II framework.

papers.title: Hubungan Perilaku Masyarakat dan Peran Kader dengan Kejadian Demam Berdarah Dengue
papers.abstract: Background: Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever (DHF) remains a major public health problem in Indonesia and is closely associated with community preventive behavior and the role of health cadres in vector control. Objective: This study aimed to analyze the relationship between community behavior and the role of health cadres with the incidence of Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever in the working area of Jalan Emas Public Health Center, Tangerang Regency. Methods: This study employed an analytical observational design with a cross-sectional approach. The population consisted of households in the working area of Jalan Emas Public Health Center. A total of 81 respondents were selected using simple random sampling. Data were collected using structured questionnaires and analyzed using Fisher’s Exact Test. Results: The results showed that most respondents had moderate dengue prevention behavior (63.0%), and more than half perceived the role of health cadres as good (58.0%). Statistical analysis revealed a significant relationship between community preventive behavior and dengue incidence (p < 0.05). A significant relationship was also found between the role of health cadres and dengue incidence (p < 0.05). Respondents with good preventive behavior and positive perceptions of cadre roles were less likely to experience dengue infection. Conclusion: Community preventive behavior and the role of health cadres are significantly associated with the incidence of Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 登革出血热(DHF)仍然是印度尼西亚的一个主要公共卫生问题,与社区预防行为和卫生干部在 媒介 控制中的作用密切相关。本研究旨在分析唐格朗县 Jalan Emas 公共卫生中心工作区登革出血热 发病率 的社区行为与卫生干部角色之间的关系。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项研究采用了横断面方法的分析观察设计。人口由 Jalan Emas 公共卫生中心工作区的家庭组成,通过简单随机抽样抽取了 81 名受访者。
elements_zh.methods: 使用结构化问卷收集数据并使用费舍尔精确检验进行分析。统计分析显示,社区预防行为与登革热发病率之间存在显着关系(p < 0.05),卫生干部的作用与登革热发病率之间也存在显着关系(p < 0.05)。
elements_zh.main_results: 结果显示,大多数受访者有中等程度的登革热预防行为(63.0%),超过一半的人认为卫生干部的作用良好(58.0%)。具有良好预防行为和对干部角色有积极看法的受访者感染登革热的可能性较小。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 社区预防行为和卫生干部的作用与登革出血热发病率显着相关。研究结果强调了社区参与和干部参与登革热预防工作的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究强调需要加强以社区为基础的登革热预防计划,并增强卫生干部在 媒介 控制中的作用,以减少登革热 媒介。这些发现可以为类似环境中的有针对性的公共卫生干预措施提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于单个公共卫生中心的工作区域,这可能会限制普遍性。由于横断面设计和小样本量,证据强度中等,但显着的关联为登革热预防策略提供了宝贵的见解。

papers.title: Extensive intraventricular hemorrhage, complicated by dengue-induced coagulopathy, initially misdiagnosed as gastroenteritis in a toddler: A case report
papers.abstract: Incomplete physical examinations especially omissions of Central nervous system (CNS) assessments remain a major cause of missed or delayed diagnoses of serious neurological conditions in febrile children with nonspecific symptoms. I report the case of a 22-month-old male initially presenting with prolonged fever, coffee-ground vomiting, nonbloody diarrhea, and recurrent convulsions, leading to a presumptive diagnosis of gastroenteritis with sepsis at Mwananyamala regional referral hospital. Despite initial management, his condition deteriorated. Subsequent evaluation at Muhimbili National Hospital revealed focal neurological deficits, hepatomegaly with jaundice, and severe coagulopathy. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated extensive intraventricular hemorrhage with obstructive hydrocephalus and multifocal acute cerebral infarcts in the setting of severe dengue-associated coagulopathy. Although an underlying vascular malformation was considered, vascular imaging was not performed and this remained unconfirmed. This case highlights the critical diagnostic challenge in pediatric care where common gastrointestinal symptoms can mask severe systemic and neurological conditions, particularly in dengue-endemic areas. It highlights the urgent need for high suspicion of central nervous system pathology, comprehensive neurological examinations, and early neuroimaging in children presenting with persistent nonspecific symptoms and new-onset seizures, crucial for timely diagnosis and management.

papers.title: IgA Dengue Virus NS1 Immune Complexes Are Associated with In Vitro Neutrophil Activation 2308886
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction Dengue virus (DENV) causes ∼400 million infections annually, with severe disease occurring more frequently during heterologous secondary infections, partly due to antibody-dependent enhancement and heightened inflammation. While IgG responses have been extensively studied, the role of circulating IgA, particularly IgA targeting non-structural protein 1 (NS1), in modulating neutrophil activation remains poorly understood. IgA immune complexes (ICs) can engage Fc receptors on neutrophils and trigger effector functions such as neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation (NETosis), but their contribution to dengue immunopathogenesis has not been fully characterized. Methods Serum samples from DENV-seropositive individuals in Puerto Rico (n = 20) were evaluated for IgA and IgG recognition of recombinant DENV-2 NS1 and envelope (E) proteins by ELISA. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the role of circulating IgA targeting non-structural protein 1 (NS1) in modulating neutrophil activation during dengue virus infection, addressing a knowledge gap in the poorly understood contribution of IgA immune complexes to dengue immunopathogenesis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used serum samples from DENV-seropositive individuals in Puerto Rico (n = 20) and neutrophils isolated from healthy donors to evaluate IgA and IgG recognition of recombinant DENV-2 NS1 and envelope proteins and assess neutrophil activation.
analysis.methods: Serum samples were evaluated for IgA and IgG recognition of recombinant DENV-2 NS1 and envelope proteins by ELISA, neutrophils were stimulated with IgA-NS1 or IgG-NS1 immune complexes for 6 hours, and NETosis was quantified using the Incucyte live cell imaging system with correlation analyses performed in GraphPad Prism.
analysis.main_results: IgA favored the recognition of NS1 over E protein (mean NS1/E ratio 1.71) compared to IgG (mean NS1/E ratio 1.09), and NETosis demonstrated a stronger association with IgA-NS1 immune complexes (R2 = 0.42, p < 0.0001) than with IgG-NS1 complexes (R2 = 0.15, p = 0.026).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that IgA-NS1 immune complexes may serve as potential modulators of neutrophil-driven inflammation in dengue, representing a distinct immunopathogenic pathway particularly relevant during heterologous DENV infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest a novel mechanism for dengue immunopathogenesis that could inform future surveillance, diagnostic strategies, and therapeutic interventions targeting IgA-NS1 interactions to mitigate neutrophil-mediated inflammation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to the small sample size (n = 20) and reliance on in vitro neutrophil stimulation, which may not fully recapitulate in vivo conditions; however, the statistical significance of the findings supports the conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the role of IgA targeting dengue virus non-structural protein 1 (NS1) in neutrophil activation. Using serum from DENV-seropositive individuals and neutrophils from healthy donors, the researchers found that IgA preferentially recognized NS1 over envelope protein compared to IgG. IgA-NS1 immune complexes induced significantly stronger neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation than IgG-NS1 complexes, suggesting a distinct immunopathogenic pathway in dengue. These findings highlight a potential mechanism for neutrophil-driven inflammation during heterologous DENV infection, warranting further investigation into therapeutic targeting of IgA-NS1 interactions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查 登革病毒 感染期间循环中靶向非结构蛋白 1 (NS1) 的 IgA 在调节中性粒细胞激活中的作用,从而解决人们对 IgA 免疫复合物对登革热免疫发病机制的贡献知之甚少的知识空白。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用波多黎各 DENV 血清阳性个体 (n = 20) 的血清样本和从健康捐赠者分离的中性粒细胞来评估重组 DENV-2 NS1 和包膜蛋白的 IgA 和 IgG 识别,并评估中性粒细胞活化。
elements_zh.methods: 通过 ELISA 评估血清样本对重组 DENV-2 NS1 和包膜蛋白的 IgA 和 IgG 识别,用 IgA-NS1 或 IgG-NS1 免疫复合物刺激中性粒细胞 6 小时,并使用 Incucyte 活细胞成像系统对 NETosis 进行定量,并在 GraphPad Prism 中进行相关分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 与 IgG(平均 NS1/E 比率 1.09)相比,IgA 比 E 蛋白更倾向于识别 NS1(平均 NS1/E 比率 1.71),并且 NETosis 证明与 IgA-NS1 免疫复合物(R2 = 0.42,p < 0.0001)的关联性强于与 IgG-NS1 复合物(R2 = 0.15,p = 0.026)的关联性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,IgA-NS1 免疫复合物可能作为登革热中中性粒细胞驱动的炎症的潜在调节剂,代表了一种独特的免疫致病途径,在异源 DENV 感染期间尤其相关。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现提出了一种登革热免疫发病机制的新机制,可以为未来的 监测、诊断策略和针对 IgA-NS1 相互作用的治疗干预措施提供信息,以减轻中性粒细胞介导的炎症。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于样本量较小(n = 20)并且依赖于体外中性粒细胞刺激,这可能无法完全重现体内条件,因此证据强度中等;然而,研究结果的统计显着性支持了结论。

papers.source_body_en: Abstract Introduction Dengue virus (DENV) causes ∼400 million infections annually, with severe disease occurring more frequently during heterologous secondary infections, partly due to antibody-dependent enhancement and heightened inflammation. While IgG responses have been extensively studied, the role of circulating IgA, particularly IgA targeting non-structural protein 1 (NS1), in modulating neutrophil activation remains poorly understood. IgA immune complexes (ICs) can engage Fc receptors on neutrophils and trigger effector functions such as neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation (NETosis), but their contribution to dengue immunopathogenesis has not been fully characterized. Methods Serum samples from DENV-seropositive individuals in Puerto Rico (n = 20) were evaluated for IgA and IgG recognition of recombinant DENV-2 NS1 and envelope (E) proteins by ELISA. Neutrophils isolated from healthy donors were stimulated for 6 hours with IgA-NS1 or IgG-NS1 immune complexes. NETosis was quantified using the Incucyte live cell imaging system. Correlation analyses were performed in GraphPad Prism. Results IgG recognized NS1 and E proteins at comparable levels, while IgA favored the recognition of NS1 over E protein. The mean NS1/E ratio was 1.09 for IgG (range 1.02—1.16) and 1.71 for IgA (range 1.18—2.10). NETosis demonstrated a stronger and more statistically significant association with IgA-NS1 ICs (R2 = 0.42, p < 0.0001) when compared to IgG-NS1 complexes (R2 = 0.15, p = 0.026). Conclusion Collectively, these findings suggest that IgA—NS1 immune complexes may serve as potential modulators of neutrophil-driven inflammation in dengue. This isotype-specific linkage to NETosis suggests a distinct immunopathogenic pathway that may be particularly relevant during heterologous DENV infection and merits further mechanistic and translational investigation. Funding Source R01AI153434 & U54MD007579 Topic Categories Viral Immunology (VIR)

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查 登革病毒 感染期间循环中靶向非结构蛋白 1 (NS1) 的 IgA 在调节中性粒细胞激活中的作用,从而解决人们对 IgA 免疫复合物对登革热免疫发病机制的贡献知之甚少的知识空白。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用波多黎各 DENV 血清阳性个体 (n = 20) 的血清样本和从健康捐赠者分离的中性粒细胞来评估重组 DENV-2 NS1 和包膜蛋白的 IgA 和 IgG 识别,并评估中性粒细胞活化。
analysis_zh.methods: 通过 ELISA 评估血清样本对重组 DENV-2 NS1 和包膜蛋白的 IgA 和 IgG 识别,用 IgA-NS1 或 IgG-NS1 免疫复合物刺激中性粒细胞 6 小时,并使用 Incucyte 活细胞成像系统对 NETosis 进行定量,并在 GraphPad Prism 中进行相关分析。
analysis_zh.main_results: 与 IgG(平均 NS1/E 比率 1.09)相比,IgA 比 E 蛋白更倾向于识别 NS1(平均 NS1/E 比率 1.71),并且 NETosis 证明与 IgA-NS1 免疫复合物(R2 = 0.42,p < 0.0001)的关联性强于与 IgG-NS1 复合物(R2 = 0.15,p = 0.026)的关联性。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,IgA-NS1 免疫复合物可能作为登革热中中性粒细胞驱动的炎症的潜在调节剂,代表了一种独特的免疫致病途径,在异源 DENV 感染期间尤其相关。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现提出了一种登革热免疫发病机制的新机制,可以为未来的 监测、诊断策略和针对 IgA-NS1 相互作用的治疗干预措施提供信息,以减轻中性粒细胞介导的炎症。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于样本量较小(n = 20)并且依赖于体外中性粒细胞刺激,这可能无法完全重现体内条件,因此证据强度中等;然而,研究结果的统计显着性支持了结论。

papers.title: Nursing education: use of clinical simulation in the care of patients with dengue fever.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To analyze how clinical simulation impacts nursing students' proficiency in clinical evaluation, decision-making, therapeutic communication, and reporting of dengue fever with warning signs within a primary health care context. METHODS: Third-term nursing undergraduates participated in the activity, which involved a standardized patient, a 45-year-old female with persistent vomiting, fever, and abdominal pain after a trip to an endemic dengue area. A structured checklist was used to assess their performance in terms of diagnostic suspicion, anamnesis, physical examination, tourniquet test, recognition of severity signs, completion of the reporting formulary, patient referral decisions, and communication with the patient. The actor received detailed instructions to ensure realism and standardization. This project followed ethical tenets and was approved by the Research Ethics Board. RESULTS: Students showed high engagement, with improvements in their logical reasoning, confidence in approaching patients, and communication. Most of them correctly identified dengue fever suspicion, although they had difficulties recognizing the warning signs, which enriched the debriefing and promoted reflection on decision-making. CONCLUSION: Clinical simulation is a powerful tool for teaching dengue fever and integrating theory and practice. Thus, it provides significant learning and strengthens the education of better-prepared nurses for qualified performance in primary healthcare.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the impact of clinical simulation on nursing students' proficiency in managing dengue fever cases within a primary health care context. The objective was to evaluate how simulation affects clinical evaluation, decision-making, therapeutic communication, and reporting of dengue fever with warning signs. Third-year nursing undergraduates participated in a simulation involving a standardized patient presenting with symptoms consistent with dengue fever. A structured checklist was used to assess their performance across several clinical domains. The results indicated high student engagement and improvements in logical reasoning, confidence, and communication. Most students correctly identified dengue fever suspicion, but difficulties in recognizing warning signs were noted, which enriched the debriefing process. The authors concluded that clinical simulation is a powerful educational tool for integrating theory and practice in dengue fever management. The study's findings suggest that simulation-based learning can strengthen nursing education for better-prepared healthcare professionals in primary care. However, the study is limited to an educational intervention without quantitative outcomes, and the evidence is moderate in strength due to its context-specific nature.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 三学期护理本科生参加了此次活动,活动涉及一名标准化患者,她是一名45岁女性,在去过登革热流行区后出现持续呕吐、发烧和腹痛。
elements_zh.methods: 使用结构化检查表来评估他们在诊断怀疑、病史、体检、止血带测试、严重性体征识别、报告处方的完成、患者转诊决定以及与患者沟通方面的表现。演员收到了详细的指示,以确保真实性和标准化。该项目遵循伦理原则,并得到研究伦理委员会的批准。
elements_zh.main_results: 学生们表现出高度的参与度,逻辑推理、接近患者的信心和沟通能力都有所提高。他们中的大多数人正确识别了登革热嫌疑,尽管他们在识别警告信号方面有困难,这丰富了汇报并促进了对决策的反思。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 临床模拟是登革热教学、理论与实践相结合的有力工具。因此,它提供了重要的学习机会,并加强了对准备更充分的护士的教育,以使其在初级保健方面取得合格的表现。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,临床模拟可以加强 登革热 的护理教育,有助于医疗保健专业人员为管理初级医疗机构中的登革热病例做好更充分的准备。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于单一的教育干预,并没有提供有关临床模拟在现实世界场景中有效性的定量数据。由于关注特定的教育背景,证据的强度适中。

papers.title: Métodos eficazes de prevenção à dengue Effective methods for dengue prevention
papers.abstract: Dengue is an arboviral disease transmitted mainly by the Aedes aegypti mosquito and represents a major public health problem in Brazil. The significant increase in cases in recent years highlights the need to strengthen disease prevention and control strategies. This study aims to identify effective methods for dengue prevention through a review of the scientific literature and official documents from the Ministry of Health. The research is characterized as qualitative, descriptive, and bibliographic. The results demonstrate that the elimination of breeding sites, health education, community participation, epidemiological surveillance, and continuous actions by vector-control agents are fundamental measures for reducing vector proliferation. It is concluded that addressing dengue depends on the integration of public authorities and the population, with prevention being the most effective strategy for reducing the incidence of the disease and its social and economic impacts.

papers.title: A Multiplex RT-LAMP-Lateral Flow Platform For Comprehensive Dengue Serotype Detection
papers.abstract: Dengue virus (DENV) is a mosquito-borne RNA virus responsible for approximately 400 million infections annually and exists as four distinct serotypes (DENV-1-4). Secondary infection with a different serotype significantly increases the risk of severe dengue, making rapid serotype differentiation critical. Current gold-standard methods, such as reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), require expensive equipment and centralized laboratories, limiting accessibility in resource-limited settings. This project aims to develop a low-cost, portable diagnostic platform that combines reverse transcription loop-mediated isothermal amplification (RT-LAMP) with a multiplex lateral flow assay (LFA) for rapid detection and differentiation of all four dengue serotypes. Serotype-specific primers are being designed and optimized for RT-LAMP. A portable heating device utilizing a fatty acid phase change material (PCM) and an Mg-Fe alloy reaction was successfully constructed to provide instrument-free amplification. The LFA mechanism was also validated by successfully immobilizing the control capture probe, demonstrating effective salt-mediated immobilization, a clear colorimetric response, and successful biotin-mediated gold nanoparticle capture. Initial testing with synthetic DENV-2 DNA demonstrated successful RT-LAMP amplification. These findings establish the feasibility of an inexpensive, field-deployable RT-LAMP-LFA platform with potential to improve early dengue diagnosis and outbreak surveillance in resource-limited settings.
papers.journal: Digital Repository at the University of Maryland (University of Maryland College Park)

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue virus (DENV) causes approximately 400 million infections annually and exists as four distinct serotypes (DENV-1–4), with secondary infection by a different serotype increasing the risk of severe dengue. Rapid serotype differentiation is critical for clinical management and outbreak control.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study developed a low-cost, portable diagnostic platform combining reverse transcription loop-mediated isothermal amplification (RT-LAMP) with a multiplex lateral flow assay (LFA) for rapid detection and differentiation of all four dengue serotypes.
analysis.methods: Serotype-specific primers were designed and optimized for RT-LAMP, and a portable heating device using a fatty acid phase change material and an Mg-Fe alloy reaction was constructed to enable instrument-free amplification. The lateral flow assay mechanism was validated by immobilizing the control capture probe, demonstrating salt-mediated immobilization, a clear colorimetric response, and successful biotin-mediated gold nanoparticle capture.
analysis.main_results: Initial testing with synthetic DENV-2 DNA demonstrated successful RT-LAMP amplification.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as establishing the feasibility of an inexpensive, field-deployable RT-LAMP-LFA platform for dengue serotype detection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This platform has potential to improve early dengue diagnosis and outbreak surveillance in resource-limited settings where access to centralized laboratories is limited.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report clinical validation, sensitivity, specificity, or performance against gold-standard methods such as RT-PCR, limiting the strength of the evidence to feasibility-level findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to address the need for rapid, accessible dengue serotype differentiation by developing a low-cost, portable RT-LAMP-LFA platform. The authors designed serotype-specific primers and constructed a portable heating device using phase change materials and an Mg-Fe alloy reaction to enable instrument-free amplification. Validation of the lateral flow assay mechanism confirmed effective probe immobilization, colorimetric response, and nanoparticle capture. Initial testing with synthetic DENV-2 DNA demonstrated successful RT-LAMP amplification, establishing feasibility. The platform is proposed to enhance early diagnosis and surveillance in resource-limited settings, though clinical validation and comparative performance data are not reported.

elements_zh.methods: 针对 RT-LAMP 设计和优化了血清型特异性引物,并构建了使用脂肪酸相变材料和镁铁合金反应的便携式加热装置,以实现免仪器扩增。通过固定对照捕获探针验证了侧流测定机制,证明了盐介导的固定、清晰的比色响应以及成功的生物素介导的金纳米颗粒捕获。
elements_zh.main_results: 合成 DENV-2 DNA 的初步测试表明 RT-LAMP 扩增成功。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为建立了一种廉价、可现场部署的 RT-LAMP-LFA 平台用于登革热血清型检测的可行性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该平台有潜力在资源有限且无法进入集中实验室的环境中改善早期登革热 诊断 和 暴发 监测。

papers.title_zh: 用于全面登革热血清型检测的多重 RT-LAMP-侧流平台
papers.source_body_en: Dengue virus (DENV) is a mosquito-borne RNA virus responsible for approximately 400 million infections annually and exists as four distinct serotypes (DENV-1-4). Secondary infection with a different serotype significantly increases the risk of severe dengue, making rapid serotype differentiation critical. Current gold-standard methods, such as reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), require expensive equipment and centralized laboratories, limiting accessibility in resource-limited settings. This project aims to develop a low-cost, portable diagnostic platform that combines reverse transcription loop-mediated isothermal amplification (RT-LAMP) with a multiplex lateral flow assay (LFA) for rapid detection and differentiation of all four dengue serotypes. Serotype-specific primers are being designed and optimized for RT-LAMP. A portable heating device utilizing a fatty acid phase change material (PCM) and an Mg-Fe alloy reaction was successfully constructed to provide instrument-free amplification. The LFA mechanism was also validated by successfully immobilizing the control capture probe, demonstrating effective salt-mediated immobilization, a clear colorimetric response, and successful biotin-mediated gold nanoparticle capture. Initial testing with synthetic DENV-2 DNA demonstrated successful RT-LAMP amplification. These findings establish the feasibility of an inexpensive, field-deployable RT-LAMP-LFA platform with potential to improve early dengue diagnosis and outbreak surveillance in resource-limited settings.

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究开发了一种低成本、便携式诊断平台,将逆转录环介导的等温扩增 (RT-LAMP) 与多重侧流测定 (LFA) 相结合,用于快速检测和区分所有四种登革热血清型。
analysis_zh.methods: 针对 RT-LAMP 设计和优化了血清型特异性引物,并构建了使用脂肪酸相变材料和镁铁合金反应的便携式加热装置,以实现免仪器扩增。通过固定对照捕获探针验证了侧流测定机制,证明了盐介导的固定、清晰的比色响应以及成功的生物素介导的金纳米颗粒捕获。
analysis_zh.main_results: 合成 DENV-2 DNA 的初步测试表明 RT-LAMP 扩增成功。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为建立了一种廉价、可现场部署的 RT-LAMP-LFA 平台用于登革热血清型检测的可行性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该平台有潜力在资源有限且无法进入集中实验室的环境中改善早期登革热 诊断 和 暴发 监测。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告针对 RT-PCR 等金标准方法的临床验证、敏感性、特异性或性能,从而将证据的强度限制在可行性水平的发现范围内。

papers.title: Cerebrospinal fluid IgM cross-reactivity among arboviruses in Japanese encephalitis patients from southern India.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: In regions where multiple arboviruses co-circulate, serological diagnosis of neuroinvasive infections is complicated by antibody cross-reactivity. IgM detection in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is often considered evidence of etiologic infection. METHODS: We retrospectively screened CSF samples positive for Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV) IgM for IgM antibodies against dengue virus (DENV), chikungunya virus (CHIKV), and West Nile virus (WNV). Clinical, laboratory, and radiological data were analyzed for a subset of confirmed cases. RESULTS: Among 60 JEV IgM-positive CSF samples, cross-reactive IgM antibodies were detected against DENV (46.7%), CHIKV (10%), and WNV (23%). Cross-reactive IgM levels were consistently lower than JEV-specific IgM. Poor clinical outcomes were associated with higher CSF leukocyte counts, protein, and lactate levels. CONCLUSIONS: CSF IgM cross-reactivity among arboviruses is frequent in Japanese encephalitis and may confound etiological diagnosis. Integrated diagnostic algorithms are required in endemic settings.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:在多种虫媒病毒共同循环的地区,神经侵袭性感染的血清学 诊断 因抗体交叉反应而变得复杂。脑脊液 (CSF) 中的 IgM 检测通常被认为是病因感染的证据。方法:我们回顾性筛查日本脑炎病毒(JEV)IgM 阳性的脑脊液样本中的 登革病毒(DENV)、基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)和西尼罗河病毒(WNV)的 IgM 抗体。对部分确诊病例的临床、实验室和放射学数据进行了分析。结果:在 60 份 JEV IgM 阳性脑脊液样本中,检测到针对 DENV(46.7%)、CHIKV(10%)和 WNV(23%)的交叉反应 IgM 抗体。交叉反应 IgM 水平始终低于 JEV 特异性 IgM。不良的临床结果与较高的脑脊液白细胞计数、蛋白质和乳酸水平相关。结论:虫媒病毒之间的脑脊液 IgM 交叉反应在日本脑炎中很常见,可能会混淆病因学 诊断。流行病环境中需要集成诊断算法。

news.content: Skip to main content Help Log in ReliefWeb Search Content Search What are you looking for? Search|t Updates Countries Disasters Organizations Topics Jobs Training Informing humanitarians worldwide 24/7 — a service provided by UN OCHA Fiji + 16 more Dengue in the Pacific: Multicountry Situation (As of 27 July 2026) Format Situation Report Sources SPCWHO Posted 27 Jul 2026 Originally published 27 Jul 2026 Attachments Download Report (PDF | 731.46 KB) HIGHLIGHTS • Since 1 January 2025, twelve dengue outbreaks have been reported across Pacific Island Countries and Areas (PICs). • During 2025, dengue outbreaks were reported in American Samoa, Cook Islands, Fiji, French Polynesia, Kiribati, Nauru, Samoa, Tonga, and Tuvalu. A total of 21,258 confirmed cases and 21 deaths were recorded across the Pacific. Fatalities were reported in Fiji (n=8), Samoa (n=7), Tonga (n=3), Nauru (n=2), and Kiribati (n=1). • Between 1 January 2026 and 2 July 2026, a total of 4 466 dengue confirmed cases, 173 hospitalisations and 3 deaths have been reported across the Pacific. • The Pacific Syndromic Surveillance System (PSSS) has reported a total of 8 723 Dengue-like Illness (DLI) cases to date, a lower trend compared to the same period last year. • In 2026 dengue outbreaks were officially declared in New Caledonia, Tonga and Shefa province Vanuatu. • The most affected countries and areas in 2026 include: Cook Islands, French Polynesia, Samoa, and New Caledonia. These account for 94% of confirmed cases. • Dengue serotype-1 (DENV-1) and serotype-2 (DENV-2) are currently in circulation. • The Cook Islands officially declared the end of its dengue outbreak on 25 May 2026. • As of 27 July 2026: o The dengue outbreak remains ongoing in Shefa Province, Vanuatu, with dengue virus serotype 1 (DENV-1) continuing to circulate. o Low levels of transmission are observed in American Samoa, Kiribati, New Caledonia, Samoa, and Tonga. o Wallis and Futuna is under monitoring, following recent reports of community transmission in both Wallis and Futuna. elements_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 新喀里多尼亚、汤加和谢法省(瓦努阿图)于2026年正式宣布暴发。库克群岛于2026年5月25日宣布结束其暴发。太平洋综合症监测系统(PSSS)迄今报告了8,723例登革热样疾病(DLI)病例,与去年同期相比呈下降趋势。瓦利斯和富图纳群岛正在根据社区 传播 报告受到监控。

news.content: Opinion Why a Rs 12,000 vaccine isn’t the silver bullet against dengue in India Clinical trials have shown that Qdenga provides long-lasting protection against all four dengue virus types in people who have had the disease. It has also been shown to protect against DENV-1 and DENV-2 among people who have never had dengue The same Aedes mosquitoes also transmit chikungunya and Zika, making integrated vector management indispensable. Eliminating mosquito breeding sites through better drainage and waste disposal must remain the first line of defence. . (Source: Getty Images/Thinkstock) Written by: Rajib Dasgupta 3 min read Jul 30, 2026 12:49 AM IST First published on: Jul 29, 2026 at 05:32 PM IST India has taken an important step in the fight against dengue. On July 21, the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation granted marketing authorisation to Qdenga , the country’s first approved dengue vaccine. Manufactured by Takeda GmbH, Germany, and marketed in India by Takeda Biopharmaceuticals, the vaccine has already been approved in 42 countries, including EU members, Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia, Argentina and Brazil. More than 24 million doses have been administered worldwide, and the vaccine has the WHO’s imprimatur. Dengue, one of the world’s fastest-spreading mosquito-borne viral diseases, is caused by four closely related virus types — DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3 and DENV-4 — and is transmitted primarily by the Aedes aegypti mosquito. Clinical trials have shown that Qdenga provides long-lasting protection against all four dengue virus types in people who have had the disease. It has also been shown to protect against DENV-1 and DENV-2 among people who have never had dengue, with particularly strong protection against DENV-2, on which the vaccine is based. Advertisement The vaccine is administered in two doses, three months apart. If the second dose is delayed, the vaccination schedule does not need to be restarted; the missed dose can be given at the earliest opportunity. The vaccine, however, is not recommended for children below six years because of lower efficacy and the relatively low prevalence of prior dengue infection in that age group. The WHO also does not recommend its use beyond 60 years until there is more evidence on safety and efficacy. It should not be administered to pregnant women, women planning pregnancy within one month of vaccination, breastfeeding mothers, immunocompromised individuals, or those receiving immunosuppressive therapies such as chemotherapy or high-dose corticosteroids. Affordability is likely to determine uptake. At an expected price of Rs 3,000-6,000 per dose, the two-dose course could cost Rs 6,000-12,000. Initial demand is, therefore, likely to come primarily from the urban middle class. Whether the vaccine should eventually be included in the Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP) is a complex question. The WHO recommends that countries consider introducing Qdenga into routine immunisation only in areas where dengue transmission is a significant public health threat. Indicators include a dengue seroprevalence exceeding 60 per cent by the age of nine years or a mean age of dengue-related hospitalisation below 16 years. India will need robust epidemiological data to determine which regions meet these criteria before considering wider public funding. Advertisement India recorded more than 2.89 lakh dengue cases and 485 deaths in 2023. Around 7,000 cases and 10 deaths have already been reported this year, with the annual surge expected during the next two or three months. you may like 1 Shashi Tharoor writes: Why an 850-seat Lok Sabha threatens Indian democracy 2 BJP’s missing diagnosis: Why couldn’t the Sangh Parivar hear the young? 3 Shashi Tharoor writes: Why an 850-seat Lok Sabha threatens Indian democracy 4 Tarique Rahman’s first foreign tour bypasses India. It’s a reset, not a rupture 5 Demolition of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University: On campus, questions about vendetta politics Vaccination, however, is only one part of the solution. The same Aedes mosquitoes also transmit chikungunya and Zika, making integrated vector management indispensable. Eliminating mosquito breeding sites through better drainage and waste disposal must remain the first line of defence. These efforts should be complemented by biological measures such as larvivorous fish, judicious use of chemical and microbial control methods, stronger coordination across government agencies, and sustained community participation. Improving public awareness and health literacy is equally important. Qdenga is a significant addition to India’s public health arsenal, but it should complement, not replace, a comprehensive strategy for controlling mosquito-borne diseases. analysis.time: Publication date: July 29, 2026. Event period: Two-year nationwide surveillance study conducted from 2023–2025.
analysis.location_and_population: Affected population: General population across much of the country, with specific mention of Bengaluru.
analysis.event: Confirmed epidemiological shift: India is entering a new phase with multiple dengue virus strains (DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3, DENV-4) circulating simultaneously, known as hyperendemic transmission. Reported by: Indian Council of Medical Research's (ICMR) Virus Research and Diagnostic Laboratory (VRDL).
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Cases: Not specified in the evidence. Risk: Increased risk of severe illness, more difficult outbreak prediction, and complicated future vaccination strategies due to hyperendemic transmission.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Investigation: Ongoing molecular surveillance study. Response: Mosquito control activities mentioned in Bengaluru. Uncertainty: Future vaccination strategies are complicated; long-term impact of hyperendemic transmission remains under study.

analysis.brief_en: India's dengue epidemic is entering a more complex phase, with multiple virus strains now circulating simultaneously across much of the country, according to a two-year nationwide surveillance study by the Indian Council of Medical Research's (ICMR) Virus Research and Diagnostic Laboratory (VRDL). This pattern, known as hyperendemic transmission, increases the risk of severe illness, makes outbreaks harder to predict, and complicates future vaccination strategies. The study, titled 'Pan-India Molecular Surveillance of Dengue Serotypes, 2023–2025,' provides a clear picture of how dengue is evolving in India and highlights the importance of these findings for outbreak management, severe disease prevention, and vaccination policy. Mosquito control activities are being implemented in affected areas like Bengaluru.

India World Sport Data Health Opinion Science Entertainment Premium Videos Podcast Photos Visual Stories Specials TH Explains eBooks TH Games Newsletter Lit For Life The Huddle Home Sci-Tech Science India’s first dengue vaccine arrives with a crucial safety caveat Qdenga could be responsible for enhancing dengue in children who have not had an infection yet in their lives. In such cases, the vaccine could simulate a primary dengue infection in the body, resulting in protection against DENV-1 and DENV-2 infections but not against a DENV-3 infectionUpdated - July 29, 2026 10:59 am IST Swaminathan S0 / 0 NewREAD LATER SEE ALL Remove The efficacy and safety of a dengue vaccine are linked to each other as two sides of the same coin, and Qdenga’s phase-3 trial data need to be understood through this lens. | Photo Credit: Getty Images India’s drug regulator just approved the country’s first dengue vaccine, Qdenga. It is designed and claimed to protect against the four serotypes of the dengue-causing virus, called DENV-1 to DENV-4. Young children as well as adults (aged 4-60 years), irrespective of whether they have had dengue before, may be vaccinated with Qdenga.More than 40 countries have already approved Qdenga, which is manufactured by the Japanese pharmaceutical company Takeda. That said, data from clinical trials that Takeda published in 2019, 2020, and 2024 on the vaccine’s efficacy raise a specific concern about its abilities. analysis.time: Published on July 27, 2026, with an update on July 29, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: India; young children and adults aged 4-60 years.
analysis.event: India's drug regulator approved the country's first dengue vaccine, Qdenga, which is designed to protect against all four dengue virus serotypes (DENV-1 to DENV-4). However, clinical trial data raise concerns about potential antibody-dependent enhancement in dengue-naive children.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Qdenga has been approved in over 40 countries. The vaccine may enhance dengue infection in children without prior exposure, potentially offering protection against DENV-1 and DENV-2 but not DENV-3.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The approval is based on phase-3 trial data from 2019, 2020, and 2024. The efficacy and safety of the vaccine are linked, and further monitoring is needed to address the antibody enhancement risk in dengue-naive individuals.

analysis.brief_en: India has approved its first dengue vaccine, Qdenga, which targets all four dengue virus serotypes. While the vaccine offers broad protection, clinical trials reveal a critical safety concern: it may enhance dengue infection in children with no prior exposure. In such cases, the vaccine could simulate a primary infection, protecting against DENV-1 and DENV-2 but leaving recipients vulnerable to DENV-3. Approved in over 40 countries, Qdenga's rollout in India highlights the need for careful screening to ensure it is administered only to individuals with prior dengue exposure. The vaccine's efficacy and safety remain closely linked, requiring ongoing surveillance to mitigate potential risks.

news.content: Home News Obituary Recipes Charity Special ಕನ್ನಡ Live TV RADIO Advertise Contact Us Matrimonial Properties Jobs General Ads Red Chillies Music Ask Dr Greetings Astrology Tribute Of Love Latest India poised to gain from global biopharma patent expiry boom Wed, Jul 29 Brain changes may be linked to sleep disorders, new study suggests Wed, Jul 29 Monsoon health: Vitamin C-rich foods can help strengthen immunity during rainy season Wed, Jul 29 Study finds heart has its own neural network that helps regulate heartbeat Wed, Jul 29 Uganda declares end of Ebola outbreak Tue, Jul 28 HPV vaccine can help eliminate cervical cancer in India: Dattatreyudu Nori Tue, Jul 28 Weekend binge drinking can silently damage liver, warn doctors Tue, Jul 28 Health India approves first dengue vaccine Qdenga for people aged 4-60 Sat, Jul 25 2026 01:09:51 PM Discover moreFilm AwardsIndian cultural goodsNews portal access Daijiworld Media Network - New Delhi New Delhi, Jul 25: India has approved its first dengue vaccine, Qdenga, marking a major milestone in the country's efforts to combat one of its most widespread mosquito-borne diseases. The Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) has granted marketing authorisation for Qdenga, a live, attenuated tetravalent dengue vaccine designed to protect against all four dengue virus serotypes—DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3 and DENV-4. The approval comes as dengue continues to pose a major public health challenge in India, particularly during the monsoon and post-monsoon seasons, when thousands of people are hospitalised every year. Developed using recombinant DNA technology, Qdenga is supplied as a freeze-dried powder that is reconstituted before administration and is given as a subcutaneous injection. According to the CDSCO approval, the vaccine is indicated for individuals aged between 4 and 60 years. It is administered in two doses of 0.5 ml each, with the second dose given three months after the first. Medical experts said one of the vaccine's key advantages is that recipients do not require routine testing to determine whether they have previously been infected with dengue before vaccination. Dr Dinesh Kumar, Director of Internal Medicine at Fortis Greater Noida, described the approval as an important development in dengue prevention. He said the vaccine offers protection against all four dengue virus serotypes and could particularly benefit people living in regions with frequent dengue outbreaks. However, he noted that vaccination decisions should be made after consultation with a healthcare professional, especially for individuals with underlying medical conditions. As Qdenga is a live-attenuated vaccine, it is generally not recommended for people with severe immune suppression or pregnant women unless future official guidelines advise otherwise. The vaccine's approval is based on extensive clinical studies evaluating its safety, immune response and effectiveness in both dengue-endemic and non-endemic countries. Trials involved participants from more than eight countries, including Brazil, Thailand and Sri Lanka, while a Phase III study was also conducted in India among people aged 4 to 60 years. Qdenga has already been approved in 42 countries, including the European Union, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand. It has also received World Health Organization (WHO) prequalification, enabling procurement by international health agencies. More than 24 million doses have been distributed globally, with post-marketing surveillance indicating a favourable safety profile. Experts emphasised that while the vaccine significantly reduces the risk of dengue and severe disease, it does not guarantee complete protection against infection. Dr Vikas Maurya, Senior Director and Head of Respiratory Medicine at Fortis Hospital, Shalimar Bagh, said dengue can range from an asymptomatic infection to life-threatening dengue haemorrhagic fever. He stressed that eliminating mosquito breeding sites remains the most effective preventive measure, while vaccination provides an additional layer of protection. Public health specialists have also reiterated that vaccination should complement, rather than replace, mosquito control measures. Preventing stagnant water accumulation, using mosquito repellents, installing window screens, wearing full-sleeved clothing, using mosquito nets and supporting local vector-control programmes remain essential in reducing dengue transmission. Dr Avi Kumar, Senior Consultant in Pulmonology at Fortis Escorts Heart Institute, said the approval of Qdenga represents an important advance in dengue prevention but should form part of a broader strategy that includes mosquito control, environmental sanitation, early diagnosis and timely medical care. Doctors also advised people to consult qualified healthcare professionals before vaccination to assess their eligibility based on age, medical history, immune status and previous dengue exposure. They stressed that anyone experiencing symptoms such as high fever, severe headache, pain behind the eyes, muscle and joint pain, nausea, vomiting, skin rash or unusual bleeding should seek immediate medical attention. Health experts said the approval of India's first dengue vaccine marks a significant scientific achievement and provides an important new tool in the country's fight against dengue, while underscoring that vaccination alone cannot eliminate the disease. news.content_title: Hillsborough County reports case of mosquito-borne dengue
news.content: The Florida Department of Health recorded the first case of dengue acquired locally in Hillsborough County this summer. Dengue fever is a mosquito-borne disease transmitted through the bite of the mosquito species aedes aegypti and aedes albopictus, which are both found in Florida. Most cases of dengue in the U.S. occur in travelers infected in areas with risk , like the Caribbean and Central and South America. In Florida, local spread is common. Typical symptoms of dengue include fever, severe headache, eye pain, muscle, joint and bone pain, bleeding, nausea, vomiting and rash, according to the health department. The joint and bone pain that some people experience gives dengue its second name, bone-break fever. Symptoms typically last 2-7 days and develop within two weeks of an infected mosquito bite. If symptoms of dengue develop, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention advise seeing a healthcare provider. There is no specific medicine to treat dengue — just rest, drinking fluids and easing symptoms with pain relief. Forty-two cases of dengue have been recorded in Florida so far this year, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The center reported 506 cases in Florida last year. Miami-Dade County accounted for over 60% of the state's cases last year. Compared to Miami-Dade's 316 cases, Hillsborough County recorded 28 and Pinellas County had eight in 2025. Hillsborough reported seven locally acquired dengue cases between July 2024 and January 2025. The health departmentand Hillsborough County Mosquito Control coordinated aerial spraying as a prevention effort. Florida is currently in the middle of mosquito season, which runs from March to October. To help prevent mosquito bites, the health department encourages residents to drain water from outside areas to reduce where mosquitoes can breed and lay eggs, cover themselves with protective clothing while outdoors and keep doors and windows closed. The department also recommends applying insect repellent that contains DEET (10-30%), picaridin, oil of lemon eucalyptus, para-menthane-diol, 2-undecanone or IR3535. For children under two months old, the department recommends mosquito netting for protection. Residents should report dead birds to the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission's website , according to the department. The Florida Department of Health regularly conducts statewide surveillance for mosquito-borne illnesses, including dengue, West Nile virus infections, Eastern equine encephalitis, St. Louis encephalitis, malaria and chikungunya. news.content_title: India approves first dengue vaccine as cases surge in South Asia
news.content: Samaan Lateef Mon, July 20, 2026 at 4:44 p.m. UTC 0 A municipal worker fumigates a market area during a dengue prevention campaign in Colombo, Sri Lanka - ISHARA S. KODIKARA/AFP via Getty Images India has approved its first dengue vaccine as cases of the mosquito-borne disease surge in South Asia. Japan’s Takeda Pharmaceutical’s dengue vaccine QDENGA has been approved by India’s drug regulator, the Centre Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO). The global threat posed by dengue has been rising for years, as climate change, urbanisation and international travel aid the spread of the mosquitoes that transmit it. The approval comes as hospitals across South Asia grapple with a surge in dengue infections. In Sri Lanka, health authorities reported 2,652 new cases on Sunday alone, taking the total to 76,044 dengue cases so far this year. At least 53 people have died. Bangladesh is also suffering a major outbreak with over 9,000 cases and 30 deaths that has piled pressure on its health system even as it battles a measles epidemic . Dengue is transmitted to humans through the bites of infected Aedes mosquitoes. Its symptoms include fever, severe muscle pain, and in severe cases, shock and internal bleeding that can be fatal. Although mortality is relatively low, outbreaks place a substantial burden on health systems. Takeda’s QDENGA jab is a live-attenuated tetravalent vaccine designed to protect against all four dengue virus serotypes. It can be given regardless of previous dengue infections. “The approval comes at a critical time for public health, as reported dengue cases in India have increased 11-fold in the past two decades,” the company said in a statement. Advertisement Dengue patients receive treatment at the District General Hospital in Sri Lanka’s Negombo city - ISHARA S. KODIKARA/AFP via Getty Images Takeda estimates that India accounts for almost one-third of the global dengue burden. The approval follows a review of global and Indian phase III trial data involving more than 20,000 participants across eight countries, including Sri Lanka, as well as 480 volunteers in India. Regulators concluded the vaccine was safe and immunogenic in adults and children aged between four and 60 years. However, the CDSCO directed the company to undertake post-marketing safety and effectiveness studies in India within six months of the vaccine’s commercial launch. QDENGA has already been approved in more than 40 countries and is WHO pre-qualified. In 2024, Takeda partnered with Indian vaccine manufacturer Biological E to manufacture up to 50 million doses annually, supporting Takeda’s target of producing 100 million doses globally each year by the end of the decade. Dr Eng Eong, a dengue expert and professor in Emerging Infectious Diseases at Duke-NUS in Singapore, told the Telegraph that it was critical for India and other dengue-affected countries to move beyond strategies reliant on vector-control. “A licenced dengue vaccine [in India] adds an important piece to the very limited public health arsenal to combat dengue,” he said. Shikha Taneja Malik, Senior Scientific Affairs Manager, Drugs for Neglected Diseases initiative, South Asia, said: “A locally manufactured, affordable vaccine could meaningfully reduce severe cases and hospital strain. But there are still specific populations such as pregnant women, newborns, and older adults who would not benefit from this vaccine.” Ms Malik said the vaccination should complement surveillance, vector control and development of new treatments to help reduce the burden of the disease. news.content: Singapore dengue cases low but increasing, may rise further with strain change Sign up now: Get ST's newsletters delivered to your inbox There were 1,180 reported cases of dengue in Singapore in the first half of 2026. PHOTO: ST FILE Zhaki Abdullah Dengue cases in Singapore dropped 54% in the first half of 2026 but rose 87.8% from April to June amid a shift to the DENV-3 serotype. A change in dominant dengue serotype often leads to more infections due to lower immunity, seen also in Malaysia and Vietnam with rising cases. Experts say Singapore’s vector control helps reduce outbreaks, but continued surveillance and rapid response are vital to manage rising dengue numbers. AI generated SINGAPORE – While dengue numbers in Singapore remain low, a change in the dominant serotype could lead to increasing infections here, said experts. According to data from the National Environment Agency (NEA), there were 1,180 reported cases of dengue here in the first half of 2026 – 54 per cent down from the 2,583 cases over the same period in 2025. Dengue cases in Singapore have fallen in recent years amid an expansion of Project Wolbachia, an initiative to control the Aedes aegypti mosquito population here. However, infections have been creeping up as the country experiences peak dengue season, which lasts from May to October. There were 770 dengue cases recorded between April and June, an 87.8 per cent increase from the 410 seen in the first quarter of the year. This comes amid a change in the predominant dengue serotype in the Republic. The DENV-3 serotype – which made up just 19.1 per cent of cases in January – comprised 59.9 per cent of infections here in June, according to the NEA’s quarterly dengue surveillance data, published on July 21. There are four dengue serotypes, or strains, which are distinct but closely related. People who are infected by one serotype can still be infected by one of the other three. A switch in the dominant serotype is typically followed by a spike in dengue cases, due to lower immunity to the new strain. Across the Causeway, a shift in serotypes has been cited as one reason for a spike in dengue infections . Earlier in the month, Malaysia’s Health Ministry said dengue numbers in the country had risen, with 42,848 recorded cases of the disease as at July 9 – a 34.8 per cent increase from the same period in 2025. The ministry said then that 34 people had died of dengue, up from 19 across the same period in 2025 . Health Minister Dzulkefly Ahmad said the ­DENV-3 serotype is now dominant in Malaysia. Meanwhile, Vietnam reported more than 50,000 cases of dengue fever in the first five months of 2026 – double the number of infections seen over the same period the previous year. A serotype switch is the most likely reason for such spikes, said Paul Tambyah, the immediate past president of the Asia Pacific Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infection. He noted that this is the case with most dengue spikes over the years, as well as other viral infections such as influenza and Covid-19, which regularly see new strains or variants. The spike in Malaysia has been concentrated around Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, where almost two-thirds of infections have occurred. However, the constant movement of people up and down the peninsula could result in spikes in Johor and Singapore, said Tambyah, who is also professor of medicine at the National University of Singapore’s Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine. “Singapore has already seen a rise in the number of dengue cases in the last quarter and this is likely to continue,” said Tambyah. He noted, however, that this may not occur if the DENV-2 serotype – which made up 67.6 per cent of cases at the start of 2026 – once again becomes predominant. Such sudden switches have happened in the past, he said, though the reasons for such occurrences are unclear. More on this topic Ooi Eng Eong – a professor in the emerging infectious diseases programme at Duke-NUS Medical School – pointed out that Singapore’s vector control programme means reduced dengue transmission and a longer interval between major outbreaks. Hence, an outbreak in Malaysia may not necessarily translate into one in Singapore, he said. Ooi said that with all four dengue serotypes circulating in Singapore, outbreaks of the disease here cannot always be attributed to low population immunity to an emerging strain. Genetic changes in each of the four strains can affect their ability to spread, and several dengue outbreaks have now been found to be caused by such genetic attributes, he added. “However, our ability to predict epidemics based on the genomic sequence of the viruses is still very much in its infancy. Research to understand the genetic changes that affect epidemic spread of dengue viruses remains much needed,” said Ooi. Tambyah said that a large spike in cases can be avoided by using the “tried and true techniques” of rapid case detection and surveillance, as well as timely and appropriate vector control. “These have worked in the past and are likely to work well again despite the serotype switch – at least in moderating the rise that we have already seen.” More on this topic Zhaki Abdullah is a correspondent at The Straits Times. He is on the health beat, in addition to occasionally covering science, environmental, tech and Muslim affairs issues. See more on Dengue fever Infectious diseases Mosquito

news.content_title: DCGI grants approval for QDENGA dengue vaccine in India
news.content: Takeda Biopharmaceuticals India Pvt Ltd has announced that the Drug Controller General of India (DCGI) has granted market authorisation for QDENGA, Takeda’s dengue vaccine, for individuals aged 4-60. This approval represents the first dengue vaccine authorised in India and permits use regardless of previous dengue exposure, without requiring pre-vaccination testing. Discover more public health Health Public Health Dengue, a mosquito-borne viral disease prevalent in over 125 countries, continues to pose a major public health challenge. India accounts for nearly one-third of the global dengue burden, with reported cases exceeding 113,000 in 2025. However, modelling analyses suggest that actual infections likely number in the tens of millions annually. Dr Mahender Nayak, Head of Intercontinental Markets at Takeda, stated, “Dengue is a growing public health challenge, and India needs sustained, evidence-based prevention. The latest seven-year data for QDENGA show continued protection against dengue infection and hospitalisation across all four serotypes; an important milestone for communities and health systems. Since its launch in 2022, QDENGA has been approved in 43 countries, with more than 32 million doses distributed globally. This approval marks an important step forward in strengthening dengue prevention in India. Building on Takeda’s 245-year heritage and more than 70 years of vaccine expertise, we remain committed to working with public health authorities, healthcare professionals, and partners to support equitable and sustainable access.” The widespread endemicity of dengue in India, combined with rapid urbanisation and climate-related factors that promote mosquito proliferation, has made dengue a year-round public health threat. Seasonal surges continue to tax healthcare systems. The disease is complex to manage as it lacks a specific treatment and can rapidly progress to severe, life-threatening complications requiring hospitalisation and intensive care. Discover more infections Company News Biological Sciences Peter Streibl, General Manager of the Southeast Asia and India Cluster at Takeda, commented, “Dengue is a shared regional challenge that requires collaboration across borders and sectors. Takeda is committed to working with governments, public health authorities, healthcare professionals, and partners across South and Southeast Asia, not only to support access to QDENGA, where approved and recommended, but also to strengthen broader dengue prevention efforts, including surveillance, awareness, vector control, and community engagement. Our aim is to contribute to sustainable, evidence-based solutions that reflect the needs of each country.” Dr Goh Choo Beng, Medical Affairs Head Southeast Asia & India Cluster, added, “India carries a substantial dengue burden, and all four dengue virus serotypes have been documented as co-circulating in several regions. QDENGA is designed to protect against all four serotypes, regardless of prior exposure. Its approval represents an important step in strengthening India’s comprehensive approach to dengue prevention, alongside vector control, surveillance, community awareness and other public health measures.” Discover more vaccine Government Agencies Drugs & Medications The Indian approval is based on results from Takeda’s global clinical development programme, which included 19 Phase 1, 2 and 3 clinical trials involving over 28,000 participants in both endemic and non-endemic regions. This programme encompassed the pivotal Phase III TIDES (DEN-301) trial, conducted with over 20,000 participants across eight countries over an extended period to evaluate the long-term safety and efficacy of QDENGA. At 12 months after the second dose, the trial demonstrated an overall vaccine efficacy of 80.2% against virologically confirmed dengue (VCD), meeting its primary endpoint. At 18 months, the study showed 90.4% efficacy against dengue-related hospitalisation, satisfying a key secondary endpoint. After 4.5 years, two doses of QDENGA provided 84.1% efficacy in preventing dengue-related hospitalisations. The vaccine has shown sustained safety and efficacy for up to seven years across all four dengue virus serotypes. Supporting data include a Phase III clinical trial (DEN-302) conducted in Indian participants, which evaluated safety and immunogenicity in individuals aged 4-60 years. This study found QDENGA to be tolerated, safe and immunogenic in healthy adults, adolescents and children. Real-world evidence generation and ongoing pharmacovigilance continue to enhance understanding of the vaccine’s safety and impact. QDENGA is a tetravalent, live-attenuated vaccine designed to protect against all four dengue virus serotypes. It is administered subcutaneously in a two-dose regimen of 0.5 mL each, with doses given three months apart. The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends QDENGA for use in dengue-endemic settings and supports its inclusion in public immunisation programmes in areas with high transmission, without the necessity for pre-vaccination screening. WHO prequalification confirms that the vaccine meets global standards for quality, safety and efficacy, enabling procurement through international agencies such as UNICEF and PAHO to support broader access. QDENGA has been approved in 43 countries across Asia, Latin America and Europe, including India, with more than 32 million doses distributed worldwide via public and private programmes. It is part of Brazil’s National Immunisation Program and is available through public programmes in Argentina, Colombia and Indonesia. Following DCGI’s approval, Takeda will continue collaboration with Indian regulatory authorities, public health stakeholders and healthcare providers to support the planning, delivery and availability of QDENGA in India

selected_identity.page_title: DCGI grants approval for QDENGA dengue vaccine in India

news.content_original: Takeda Biopharmaceuticals India Pvt Ltd has announced that the Drug Controller General of India (DCGI) has granted market authorisation for QDENGA, Takeda’s dengue vaccine, for individuals aged 4-60. This approval represents the first dengue vaccine authorised in India and permits use regardless of previous dengue exposure, without requiring pre-vaccination testing. Discover more public health Health Public Health Dengue, a mosquito-borne viral disease prevalent in over 125 countries, continues to pose a major public health challenge. India accounts for nearly one-third of the global dengue burden, with reported cases exceeding 113,000 in 2025. However, modelling analyses suggest that actual infections likely number in the tens of millions annually. Dr Mahender Nayak, Head of Intercontinental Markets at Takeda, stated, “Dengue is a growing public health challenge, and India needs sustained, evidence-based prevention. The latest seven-year data for QDENGA show continued protection against dengue infection and hospitalisation across all four serotypes; an important milestone for communities and health systems. Since its launch in 2022, QDENGA has been approved in 43 countries, with more than 32 million doses distributed globally. This approval marks an important step forward in strengthening dengue prevention in India. Building on Takeda’s 245-year heritage and more than 70 years of vaccine expertise, we remain committed to working with public health authorities, healthcare professionals, and partners to support equitable and sustainable access.” The widespread endemicity of dengue in India, combined with rapid urbanisation and climate-related factors that promote mosquito proliferation, has made dengue a year-round public health threat. Seasonal surges continue to tax healthcare systems. The disease is complex to manage as it lacks a specific treatment and can rapidly progress to severe, life-threatening complications requiring hospitalisation and intensive care. Discover more infections Company News Biological Sciences Peter Streibl, General Manager of the Southeast Asia and India Cluster at Takeda, commented, “Dengue is a shared regional challenge that requires collaboration across borders and sectors. Takeda is committed to working with governments, public health authorities, healthcare professionals, and partners across South and Southeast Asia, not only to support access to QDENGA, where approved and recommended, but also to strengthen broader dengue prevention efforts, including surveillance, awareness, vector control, and community engagement. Our aim is to contribute to sustainable, evidence-based solutions that reflect the needs of each country.” Dr Goh Choo Beng, Medical Affairs Head Southeast Asia & India Cluster, added, “India carries a substantial dengue burden, and all four dengue virus serotypes have been documented as co-circulating in several regions. QDENGA is designed to protect against all four serotypes, regardless of prior exposure. Its approval represents an important step in strengthening India’s comprehensive approach to dengue prevention, alongside vector control, surveillance, community awareness and other public health measures.” Discover more vaccine Government Agencies Drugs & Medications The Indian approval is based on results from Takeda’s global clinical development programme, which included 19 Phase 1, 2 and 3 clinical trials involving over 28,000 participants in both endemic and non-endemic regions. This programme encompassed the pivotal Phase III TIDES (DEN-301) trial, conducted with over 20,000 participants across eight countries over an extended period to evaluate the long-term safety and efficacy of QDENGA. At 12 months after the second dose, the trial demonstrated an overall vaccine efficacy of 80.2% against virologically confirmed dengue (VCD), meeting its primary endpoint. At 18 months, the study showed 90.4% efficacy against dengue-related hospitalisation, satisfying a key secondary endpoint. After 4.5 years, two doses of QDENGA provided 84.1% efficacy in preventing dengue-related hospitalisations. The vaccine has shown sustained safety and efficacy for up to seven years across all four dengue virus serotypes. Supporting data include a Phase III clinical trial (DEN-302) conducted in Indian participants, which evaluated safety and immunogenicity in individuals aged 4-60 years. This study found QDENGA to be tolerated, safe and immunogenic in healthy adults, adolescents and children. Real-world evidence generation and ongoing pharmacovigilance continue to enhance understanding of the vaccine’s safety and impact. QDENGA is a tetravalent, live-attenuated vaccine designed to protect against all four dengue virus serotypes. It is administered subcutaneously in a two-dose regimen of 0.5 mL each, with doses given three months apart. The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends QDENGA for use in dengue-endemic settings and supports its inclusion in public immunisation programmes in areas with high transmission, without the necessity for pre-vaccination screening. WHO prequalification confirms that the vaccine meets global standards for quality, safety and efficacy, enabling procurement through international agencies such as UNICEF and PAHO to support broader access. QDENGA has been approved in 43 countries across Asia, Latin America and Europe, including India, with more than 32 million doses distributed worldwide via public and private programmes. It is part of Brazil’s National Immunisation Program and is available through public programmes in Argentina, Colombia and Indonesia. Following DCGI’s approval, Takeda will continue collaboration with Indian regulatory authorities, public health stakeholders and healthcare providers to support the planning, delivery and availability of QDENGA in India

news.content: Why India's First Dengue Vaccine Marks a Public Health Milestone As climate change, rapid urbanisation and population growth fuel the spread of dengue, CDSCO's approval of Takeda's Qdenga marks a significant step in India's disease prevention strategy. With reported dengue cases rising 11-fold over the past two decades, doctors say the country's first dengue vaccine could reduce severe disease, hospitalisations and deaths, while calling for its eventual inclusion in the National Immunisation Programme. - Exclusive It's free content, simply login/signup to unlock Get in-depth Industry Insights and Analysis through our “Exclusive” content, presented to you by our esteemed panel of writers, for free By continuing, you agree to the T&C, Privacy Policy and Prohibited Content Policy.
